backlog.title: The Agency 2027 Red Paper: 84% of agents across 180 locations say too early to tell if AI wealth is lifting business; SF sales over $20M: 6 in 2026 (to early Aug) vs 1 in all of 2025; over $5M: 129 vs 113
backlog.angle: Luxury and AI-IPO wealth; pair with Realtor.com luxury backlog item

backlog.title: Payments outpace pay: Freddie Mac 30-yr 7.11% (week ending Nov 12) vs 6.24% a year ago; P&I on $416,700 median with 20% down ~$2,243 vs ~$2,050 (+$192, ~9%) while hourly earnings rose 3.1% to $38.00; Oct jobs +165,000, unemployment 4.1%; existing-home sales 3.75M pace, lowest since Aug 2010
backlog.angle: Wages vs payments affordability squeeze; rates angle used Nov 11-12, hold a few days

backlog.title: Redfin generational analysis: older millennials who bought in 2020-21 briefly beat boomers on affordability; millennials buying at 40 spend ~35% of income on housing vs 27% at 30; boomers in early '80s often 60%+; 43% of millennials vs 31% of boomers unlikely to move due to prices

ARA forms AI Task Force to push 'licensee-in-the-loop' laws in all 50 states: AI acting for consumers must be supervised by a named licensee (name + license number), licensee reviews every offer/counter, fiduciary duty extends to AI work; bills possible late 2026/Jan 2027; chaired by Dmitriy Kruglyak
backlog.angle: What AI-agent rules could mean for licensees; no political opinion

backlog.title: Cook County tax sale resumes in Dec 2026 with 9,481 eligible properties, fewest since 1994 and first time under 10,000 in 30+ years (vs 14,000+ expected in March); 2,700+ owe under $1,000
backlog.angle: Chicago angle; fewer distressed tax-delinquent homes, pair with foreclosure data after Nov 18

backlog.title: NY Fed Q3 2026 household debt: ~5.0% of balances in some stage of delinquency (+0.3 pp), 90+ day share 3.4%; mortgage serious delinquency 1.1% (+0.1 pp), mortgage transition into serious delinquency 1.6% (from 1.5%); auto 5.7%, student loans 10.9%
backlog.angle: Mortgage stress creeping up; pair with ATTOM October foreclosure report when out, verify against NY Fed original

backlog.title: Financial Health Network report 'Rising Costs, Shrinking Coverage' (Nov 10 2026): 54% of households at least somewhat confident insurance would cover them, lowest since 2018; home insurance share of income 1.2% (2000) to 2.1% (2022); non-renewals rose in 35 states 2018-2023; insurer-of-last-resort residential policies +77% 2019-2024; CA FAIR Plan +152% since Sept 2022; Chicago Fed research links $1,000 premium increase to higher mortgage denials
backlog.angle: Insurance costs as a deal risk; no Illinois figures
